tools.name: get_user_profile
tools.description: Returns the authenticated account’s own user profile using the provided account_id, serving cached data unless refresh=true triggers a refetch and cache update; the response is the stored user record for that account context. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if account_id is missing/invalid, NOT_FOUND if the account_id does not exist locally, UNAUTHORIZED if the account is not usable for API access, and RATE_LIMITED if the upstream X quota for profile fetches is exhausted (including when refresh=true).

account_id.description: Local authenticated account id to use as context for fetching the profile.

refresh.description: Whether to force-refresh the profile from X instead of using cached data.

tools.name: get_user_by_screen_name
tools.description: Looks up a user by screen_name (without @) and returns the locally stored user record, optionally using account_id for authenticated resolution and refresh=true to refetch and update the cache. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if screen_name is empty/invalid or account_id (when provided) is malformed, NOT_FOUND if the user cannot be resolved, UNAUTHORIZED if the provided account_id is not permitted/usable for lookups, and RATE_LIMITED when an upstream refresh is required but X rate limits prevent it.

screen_name.description: X/Twitter handle without the leading @.

account_id.description: Local authenticated account id to use for lookup/refresh context.

refresh.description: Whether to force-refresh the user from X instead of using cached data.

tools.name: get_user_by_id
tools.description: Fetches and returns a single user record identified by either user_id (local id) or x_user_id (X id), optionally using account_id as authenticated context and refresh=true to refetch and update cached fields. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if neither identifier is provided, if both are provided but refer to different users, or if any provided id fails its format checks; raises NOT_FOUND if no matching user exists (or the referenced account_id does not exist), UNAUTHORIZED if the given account_id cannot be used to query X, and RATE_LIMITED if refresh=true triggers an upstream call that exceeds quota.

user_id.description: Local user id to fetch.

account_id.description: Local authenticated account id to use for lookup/refresh context.

refresh.description: Whether to force-refresh the user from X instead of using cached data.

tools.name: get_user_followers
tools.description: Returns a paged list of follower users for the target specified by user_x_id or screen_name, using account_id as the authenticated context; results are limited by limit (1–200) and advanced with cursor from the prior page, and refresh=true forces rebuilding the follower edges from X before returning. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if neither user_x_id nor screen_name is provided, if limit is out of range, or if cursor/account_id is malformed; raises NOT_FOUND if the target user cannot be resolved, UNAUTHORIZED if account_id is not permitted/usable for this graph query, and RATE_LIMITED when refresh=true (or a cache miss) requires upstream calls that exceed quota.

user_x_id.description: X user id (users.x_id) whose followers should be retrieved.

screen_name.description: Screen name whose followers should be retrieved (alternative to user_x_id).

account_id.description: Local authenticated account id to use as context for the request.

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page of results.

refresh.description: Whether to force-refresh follower edges from X instead of using cached relationships.

tools.name: get_user_following
tools.description: Returns a paged list of users the target (user_x_id or screen_name) is following, using account_id as context; results honor limit (1–200) and cursor-based pagination, and refresh=true forces refetch of following edges from X before responding. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for missing/invalid target, out-of-range limit, or malformed cursor/account_id; raises NOT_FOUND if the target user cannot be resolved, UNAUTHORIZED if account_id is not usable for the request, and RATE_LIMITED when upstream calls are required and X quota is exhausted.

user_x_id.description: X user id (users.x_id) whose following list should be retrieved.

screen_name.description: Screen name whose following list should be retrieved (alternative to user_x_id).

account_id.description: Local authenticated account id to use as context for the request.

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page of results.

refresh.description: Whether to force-refresh following edges from X instead of using cached relationships.

tools.name: get_user_followers_you_know
tools.description: Computes and returns a paged list of “common followers” between the provided account_id (“you”) and the target user (user_x_id or screen_name), limited by limit (1–200) and paged with cursor; refresh=true forces refetch of the underlying follower data from X before computing results. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if the target is missing/invalid, if limit/cursor/account_id is malformed, or if account_id is missing; raises NOT_FOUND if the account_id does not exist locally or the target user cannot be resolved, UNAUTHORIZED if the account context cannot be used to access the necessary graph data, and RATE_LIMITED if refresh/lookup requires upstream calls that exceed quota.

screen_name.description: Screen name to compute common followers for (alternative to user_x_id).

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page of results.

refresh.description: Whether to force-refresh underlying follower data from X instead of using cached relationships.

screen_name.description: Screen name whose subscriptions should be retrieved (alternative to user_x_id).

refresh.description: Whether to force-refresh subscription edges from X instead of using cached relationships.

Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for missing/invalid account_id, empty/overlong text, malformed media items, or invalid combinations (e.g., both reply_to_tweet_x_id and quote_tweet_x_id when not supported), NOT_FOUND if a referenced reply/quote tweet or media_id cannot be resolved, UNAUTHORIZED if the account cannot post, CONFLICT if posting is refused due to an account/tweet state constraint (e.g., duplicate/blocked action), and RATE_LIMITED if posting exceeds allowed write quota.

account_id.description: Local authenticated account id to post the tweet as.

text.description: Tweet text content.

reply_to_tweet_x_id.description: X tweet id to reply to.

media.description: Media attachments to include with the tweet.

alt_text.description: Alt text for the attached media.

tools.description: Deletes the tweet identified by tweet_id (numeric X id) using account_id as the authenticated context and returns a confirmation of deletion (and updates local storage accordingly). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if account_id or tweet_id fails its format requirements, NOT_FOUND if the tweet does not exist or cannot be accessed in this context, UNAUTHORIZED if the account is not permitted to delete the tweet, CONFLICT if the tweet is already deleted or cannot be deleted due to current state, and RATE_LIMITED if the delete request exceeds upstream quota.

account_id.description: Authenticated account context to use when deleting the tweet.

tweet_id.description: The X/Twitter tweet ID (x_id) to delete.

tools.name: get_tweet_details
tools.description: Returns the full stored details for tweet_id (numeric X id) using account_id as the authenticated context, including any locally persisted enrichments available for that tweet. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if account_id or tweet_id is malformed, NOT_FOUND if the tweet cannot be found/resolved, UNAUTHORIZED if the account cannot access the tweet details, and RATE_LIMITED if fetching requires upstream calls and X quota is exhausted.

account_id.description: Authenticated account context to use when fetching tweet details.

tweet_id.description: The X/Twitter tweet ID (x_id) to fetch details for.

tools.name: create_poll_tweet
tools.description: Creates a new tweet for the given authenticated account and attaches a poll with 2–4 choices and the provided duration, returning the created tweet record (including its X/Twitter tweet ID) and poll metadata. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if account_id is not a valid authenticated context, if choices is not 2–4 items, or if duration_minutes is < 1 (or any required field is missing). Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the account context cannot act, QUOTA_EXCEEDED if posting is rate-limited, and CONFLICT if the tweet cannot be created in the current account state.

account_id.description: Authenticated account context to use when creating the tweet.

text.description: Tweet text to post along with the poll.

tools.name: vote_on_poll
tools.description: Casts a vote on the poll contained in the specified tweet on behalf of the authenticated account and returns the updated poll state as observed after voting. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if choice_index is negative or required fields are missing, NOT_FOUND if tweet_id does not exist or does not reference a tweet with a poll, and CONFLICT if the vote is not allowed (e.g., poll is closed or the account has already voted and revoting is not supported). Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the account context cannot act and QUOTA_EXCEEDED if voting is rate-limited.

account_id.description: Authenticated account context to use when voting on the poll.

tweet_id.description: The X/Twitter tweet ID (x_id) containing the poll to vote on.

choice_index.description: Zero-based index of the poll choice to vote for.

tools.name: favorite_tweet
tools.description: Favorites (likes) the specified tweet on behalf of the authenticated account and returns the resulting favorite state for that tweet. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if parameters are malformed, NOT_FOUND if tweet_id does not exist, and CONFLICT if the tweet cannot be favorited in its current state (for example, already favorited when duplicates are not accepted). Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the account context cannot act and QUOTA_EXCEEDED if the action is rate-limited.

account_id.description: Authenticated account context to use when favoriting the tweet.

tweet_id.description: The X/Twitter tweet ID (x_id) to favorite.

tools.name: unfavorite_tweet
tools.description: Removes the authenticated account’s favorite (like) from the specified tweet and returns the resulting favorite state for that tweet. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if parameters are malformed, NOT_FOUND if tweet_id does not exist, and CONFLICT if there is no existing favorite to remove or the tweet cannot transition to an unfavorited state. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the account context cannot act and QUOTA_EXCEEDED if the action is rate-limited.

account_id.description: Authenticated account context to use when removing the favorite.

tweet_id.description: The X/Twitter tweet ID (x_id) to unfavorite.

tools.name: bookmark_tweet
tools.description: Adds the specified tweet to the authenticated account’s bookmarks and returns the resulting bookmark state for that tweet. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if parameters are malformed and NOT_FOUND if tweet_id does not exist. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the account context cannot act, QUOTA_EXCEEDED if bookmarking is rate-limited, and CONFLICT if the tweet is already bookmarked and duplicates are not accepted.

account_id.description: Authenticated account context to use when bookmarking the tweet.

tweet_id.description: The X/Twitter tweet ID (x_id) to bookmark.

tools.name: delete_bookmark

Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if parameters are malformed and NOT_FOUND if tweet_id does not exist. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the account context cannot act, QUOTA_EXCEEDED if the operation is rate-limited, and CONFLICT if the tweet is not currently bookmarked.

account_id.description: Authenticated account context to use when removing the bookmark.

tweet_id.description: The X/Twitter tweet ID (x_id) to remove from bookmarks.

tools.name: delete_all_bookmarks
tools.description: Deletes all bookmarks for the authenticated account and returns a summary of the deletion (for example, how many bookmarks were removed). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if account_id is malformed or missing and UNAUTHORIZED if the account context cannot act. Raises QUOTA_EXCEEDED if the operation is rate-limited and CONFLICT if bookmarks cannot be cleared in the current account state.

account_id.description: Authenticated account to delete bookmarks for.

tools.name: get_repo_metadata
tools.description: Returns the repository snapshot metadata object, optionally reduced to only the requested top-level fields. If `fields` is provided, we only include fields that exist in the metadata and refuse requests where `fields` is not an array of strings. We also refuse requests that ask for no usable fields (for example, an empty `fields` list), because there would be nothing to return.

fields.description: List of metadata fields to include. If omitted, returns the full metadata object.

tools.name: list_issues_prs
tools.description: Returns a list of issues and pull requests from the snapshot, or a single entry when `number` is provided, optionally filtered by `state` and/or opener `user` and optionally reduced to selected fields. We refuse requests with an invalid `state`, a non-integer `number`/`limit`, a `limit` that is not positive, or a `fields` value that is not an array of strings. When `number` is provided, we refuse the request if that issue/PR number does not exist in the snapshot.

user.description: Filter by the login of the user who opened the issue/PR.

number.description: Retrieve a specific issue/PR by its number.

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (default 20).

fields.description: List of fields to include for each entry.

tools.name: list_commits
tools.description: Returns a list of commits from the snapshot, or a single commit when `sha` is provided, optionally filtered by `author` and/or a time window and optionally reduced to selected fields. We refuse requests where `since`/`until` are not valid ISO date-time strings, where `since` is after `until`, where `limit` is not a positive integer, or where `fields` is not an array of strings. When `sha` is provided, we refuse the request if that commit SHA is not present in the snapshot.

since.description: Only include commits after this ISO timestamp.

until.description: Only include commits before this ISO timestamp.

sha.description: Retrieve a specific commit by its SHA.

limit.description: Maximum number of commits to return (default 20).

fields.description: List of fields to include for each commit.

tools.name: list_root_contents
tools.description: Returns entries from the repository root snapshot, optionally filtered by `entry_type` and/or `path_prefix` and optionally reduced to selected fields. We refuse requests with an `entry_type` other than `file` or `dir`, a `limit` that is not a positive integer, or a `fields` value that is not an array of strings. We also refuse requests where `path_prefix` is not a string.

entry_type.description: Filter entries by type (file or dir).

path_prefix.description: Only include entries whose path starts with this prefix.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default 20).

fields.description: List of fields to include for each entry.

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: Returns a list of available terminal commands from the snapshot, optionally filtered by `category`, exact `name`, or `name_prefix`, and optionally reduced to the selected fields. We refuse requests that include any parameters other than the documented ones, a `limit` that is not a positive integer, or a `fields` list containing anything other than `name`, `description`, or `category`. If both `name` and `name_prefix` are provided, we refuse the request because those filters conflict.

name.description: Filter commands by exact command name.

name_prefix.description: Only include commands whose name starts with this prefix.

limit.description: Maximum number of commands to return (default 20).

fields.description: List of fields to include for each command.

tools.name: get_command
tools.description: Returns the command definition that matches the provided command `name`. We refuse requests missing `name` or where `name` is not a string. We also refuse the request if no command with that exact name exists in the snapshot.

name.description: The name of the command to retrieve.

tools.name: list_commands_by_category
tools.description: Returns all commands whose category matches the provided `category`. We refuse requests missing `category` or where `category` is not a string. We also refuse the request if the category does not exist in the snapshot (meaning it would match no commands).

category.description: The category to filter commands by (e.g., "File Management", "Networking").

tools.name: get_toolset
tools.description: Returns one toolset definition from the snapshot (name, description, tools, allowed shell operators, default directory), optionally reduced to only the requested fields. We refuse requests that include any parameters other than the documented ones, a `fields` list containing unknown field names, or a `fields` value that is not an array. If `toolset_name` is provided, we refuse the request when that toolset does not exist in the snapshot.

toolset_name.description: Retrieve a specific toolset by its toolset_name.

fields.description: List of fields to include. If omitted, returns the full toolset object.

tools.name: get_security_rules
tools.description: Returns the terminal security rules snapshot, optionally reduced to only the requested fields. We refuse requests that include any parameters other than the documented ones, a `fields` list containing unknown field names, or a `fields` value that is not an array. We also refuse requests that ask for no usable fields (for example, an empty `fields` list), because there would be nothing to return.

fields.description: List of fields to include. If omitted, returns the full security rules object.

tools.name: get_readme
tools.description: Returns the repository README contents either as the raw source (`raw`) or as plain text (`text`). We refuse requests that include any parameters other than the documented ones or a `format` other than `raw` or `text`. We also refuse the request if the README content is not available in the snapshot.

format.description: Return format for the README contents.

tools.name: init-n8n
tools.description: Creates and stores a connection record for an n8n instance using the provided base URL, auth method, optional secret reference, and owner, and returns the created instance object (including its new instance_id). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if required fields are missing, IDs do not match the required n8n_* ULID patterns, or auth_secret_ref is provided for an incompatible auth_type. Raises NOT_FOUND if owner_user_id does not exist, CONFLICT if an instance connection for the same base_url already exists for that owner, and FORBIDDEN if the caller is not allowed to provision instances for the specified owner.

display_name.description: Human-friendly name for the connected n8n instance.

base_url.description: Base URL of the n8n instance (e.g., https://n8n.example.com).

auth_type.description: Authentication method used to connect to the n8n instance.

auth_secret_ref.description: Reference to a stored secret containing credentials/token for the chosen auth_type.

owner_user_id.description: Owner user id for this instance connection (ULID with n8n_usr_ prefix).

limit.description: Maximum number of workflows to return.

user_id.description: ULID of the user to retrieve.

user_id.description: ULID of the user to delete.

instance_id.description: n8n instance id (ULID, e.g., n8n_inst_01H8…).

credential_id.description: Credential id to delete (stored in ops_and_metadata.id for record_type='credential', ULID typically n8n_op_01H8…).

instance_id.description: n8n instance id (ULID, e.g., n8n_inst_01H8…).

type_name.description: Credential type name to fetch schema for (e.g., 'githubApi').

instance_id.description: n8n instance id (ULID, e.g., n8n_inst_01H8…).

instance_id.description: n8n instance id (ULID, e.g., n8n_inst_01H8…).

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor to fetch the next page.

tools.name: authenticate
tools.description: Starts or resumes the Google OAuth2 flow for the given local account and returns an authorization URL to send the user to, using the provided redirect_uri and optional scopes. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if account_id does not match the required format, redirect_uri is missing/invalid, or scopes contains non-strings. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if the caller is not allowed to initiate OAuth for the account and QUOTA_EXCEEDED if OAuth initiations are rate-limited for the account or client.

account_id.description: Local account ID to start/continue OAuth for.

redirect_uri.description: OAuth redirect/callback URI that Google will send the auth code to.

scopes.description: Requested Google OAuth scopes for Tasks access.

tools.name: set-auth-code
tools.description: Exchanges the Google OAuth authorization code for tokens and persists/updates the account’s OAuth2 connection state, returning the updated connection details (and enabling subsequent Google Tasks calls on behalf of the user). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if account_id/code/redirect_uri are missing or malformed, or if redirect_uri does not match the one used to initiate the flow. Raises NOT_FOUND if the account does not exist, CONFLICT if the account is not currently in an OAuth-in-progress state, and UNAUTHORIZED/QUOTA_EXCEEDED if the caller cannot modify the account or token exchanges are throttled.

account_id.description: Local account ID whose OAuth connection should be updated with the received code.

code.description: Authorization code received from the Google OAuth redirect.

redirect_uri.description: Redirect/callback URI used in the original OAuth request (must match for code exchange).

Raises NOT_FOUND if the account does not exist and UNAUTHORIZED if the caller cannot access the account’s tasklists.

account_id.description: Local account ID whose tasklists should be listed.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor for fetching the next page.

tools.name: create_page
tools.description: Creates a new Notion page under the specified parent (page, database, or workspace) using the selected integration, optionally setting title/properties/icon/cover and creating initial child blocks; returns the created Notion page object as mirrored locally. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if parent_type is invalid, if parent_notion_id is missing when parent_type is page/database, or if provided Notion payload shapes are not objects/arrays as required; raises UNAUTHORIZED if the integration_id is unknown/disabled, FORBIDDEN if the integration cannot write to the target parent, NOT_FOUND if the specified parent does not exist or is not shared with the integration, and RATE_LIMITED if Notion or this service rejects the request due to quota.

integration_id.description: Local integration id to use for the Notion request.

parent_type.description: Type of parent container where the page will be created.

parent_notion_id.description: Notion id of the parent page/database (required when parent_type is page or database).

title.description: Plain text title for the new page.

properties.description: Notion page properties payload to set on creation (Notion API shape).

icon.description: Notion icon object to set on the page (Notion API shape).

cover.description: Notion cover object to set on the page (Notion API shape).

content_blocks.description: Optional list of Notion block objects to create as children of the new page.

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Retrieves a Notion page by notion_page_id using the given integration and returns the page object (and updates/uses the local mirror for that page). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if notion_page_id is missing/invalid, UNAUTHORIZED if the integration_id is unknown/disabled, FORBIDDEN if the integration does not have access to the page, NOT_FOUND if the page does not exist or is not shared with the integration, and RATE_LIMITED when upstream or service quotas are exceeded.

integration_id.description: Local integration id to use for the Notion request.

tools.name: update_page
tools.description: Updates an existing Notion page’s properties and/or icon/cover and can set its archived state; returns the updated Notion page object as mirrored locally. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if the update payload is malformed (e.g., non-object properties, invalid types), UNAUTHORIZED if the integration_id is unknown/disabled, FORBIDDEN if the integration lacks permission to edit the page, NOT_FOUND if the page does not exist or is not shared with the integration, CONFLICT if the requested state transition is refused by Notion (e.g., attempting to modify fields that are not editable in the page’s current state), and RATE_LIMITED if quotas are exceeded.

integration_id.description: Local integration id to use for the Notion request.

properties.description: Notion page properties payload to update (Notion API shape).

archived.description: Whether the page should be archived in Notion.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description: Returns the authenticated GitHub user’s profile details for the token/session this service is using. It refuses requests when no valid GitHub authentication is available, or when the token does not have permission to read the current user’s profile.

tools.name: get_teams
tools.description: Get details of the teams the user is a member of. Limited to organizations accessible with current credentials

user.description: Username to get teams for. If not provided, uses the authenticated user.

tools.name: get_team_members
tools.description: Get member usernames of a specific team in an organization. Limited to organizations accessible with current credentials

org.description: Organization login (owner) that contains the team.

tools.name: list_issue_types
tools.description: Lists the issue types available for repositories owned by the specified organization owner. It refuses requests with a missing or empty owner, when the owner does not exist or is not an organization, or when the service cannot access that organization’s issue-type configuration (for example due to insufficient permissions).

owner.description: The organization owner of the repository

tools.name: search_repositories
tools.description: Searches GitHub repositories using the provided query and returns a paginated list of matching repositories, optionally in minimal form. It refuses requests with a missing or empty query, invalid pagination values (page < 1, perPage < 1, perPage > 100), or unsupported sort/order values. It also refuses queries GitHub rejects (for example malformed search qualifiers) or searches the current credentials are not allowed to execute.

minimal_output.description: Return minimal repository information (default: true). When false, returns full GitHub API repository objects.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

query.description: Repository search query. Examples: 'machine learning in:name stars:>1000 language:python', 'topic:react', 'user:facebook'. Supports advanced search syntax for precise filtering.

sort.description: Sort repositories by field, defaults to best match

tools.name: search_code
tools.description: Runs a GitHub code search for the provided query and returns a paginated list of matching code results. It refuses requests with a missing or empty query, invalid pagination values (page < 1, perPage < 1, perPage > 100), or unsupported sort/order values (including sort values GitHub does not allow for code search). It also refuses queries GitHub rejects (for example malformed qualifiers or disallowed combinations) or searches the current credentials are not allowed to execute.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

query.description: Search query using GitHub's powerful code search syntax. Examples: 'content:Skill language:Java org:github', 'NOT is:archived language:Python OR language:go', 'repo:github/github-mcp-server'. Supports exact matching, language filters, path filters, and more.

tools.name: search_issues
tools.description: Searches GitHub issues using the provided query (scoped to issues) and returns a paginated list of matching issues, optionally narrowed to a specific repository when owner and repo are provided. It refuses requests with a missing or empty query, invalid pagination values (page < 1, perPage < 1, perPage > 100), unsupported sort/order values, or when only one of owner/repo is supplied. It also refuses repository scoping when the owner/repo does not exist or is not accessible to the current credentials, and refuses queries GitHub rejects as invalid.

owner.description: Optional repository owner. If provided with repo, only issues for this repository are listed.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

query.description: Search query using GitHub issues search syntax

repo.description: Optional repository name. If provided with owner, only issues for this repository are listed.

sort.description: Sort field by number of matches of categories, defaults to best match

tools.name: search_pull_requests
tools.description: Searches GitHub pull requests using the provided query (scoped to PRs) and returns a paginated list of matching pull requests, optionally narrowed to a specific repository when owner and repo are provided. It refuses requests with a missing or empty query, invalid pagination values (page < 1, perPage < 1, perPage > 100), unsupported sort/order values, or when only one of owner/repo is supplied. It also refuses repository scoping when the owner/repo does not exist or is not accessible to the current credentials, and refuses queries GitHub rejects as invalid.

owner.description: Optional repository owner. If provided with repo, only pull requests for this repository are listed.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

query.description: Search query using GitHub pull request search syntax

repo.description: Optional repository name. If provided with owner, only pull requests for this repository are listed.

sort.description: Sort field by number of matches of categories, defaults to best match

tools.name: search_users
tools.description: Searches GitHub users using the provided query (scoped to users) and returns a paginated list of matching accounts. It refuses requests with a missing or empty query, invalid pagination values (page < 1, perPage < 1, perPage > 100), or unsupported sort/order values. It also refuses queries GitHub rejects (for example malformed qualifiers) or searches the current credentials are not allowed to execute.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

query.description: User search query. Examples: 'john smith', 'location:seattle', 'followers:>100'. Search is automatically scoped to type:user.

sort.description: Sort users by number of followers or repositories, or when the person joined GitHub.

tools.name: list_branches
tools.description: Lists branches for the specified repository and returns a paginated set of branch summaries. It refuses requests with missing or empty owner/repo, invalid pagination values (page < 1, perPage < 1, perPage > 100), or when the repository does not exist. It also refuses access when the repository is private or otherwise not readable by the current credentials.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

tools.name: list_tags
tools.description: Lists git tags for the specified repository and returns a paginated set of tag references. It refuses requests with missing or empty owner/repo, invalid pagination values (page < 1, perPage < 1, perPage > 100), or when the repository does not exist. It also refuses access when the repository is private or otherwise not readable by the current credentials.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

tools.name: get_tag
tools.description: Returns details for a specific git tag in the specified repository. It refuses requests with missing or empty owner/repo/tag, when the repository does not exist or is not readable by the current credentials, or when the named tag cannot be found in that repository. It also refuses tag names that GitHub treats as invalid references.

tag.description: Tag name

tools.name: list_releases
tools.description: Lists the releases we’ve snapshotted for the specified repository and returns a paginated set of release records. It refuses requests missing an owner or repo, or with pagination values outside the supported range (page < 1, perPage < 1, or perPage > 100). It also refuses requests for repositories that don’t exist or aren’t accessible to the current integration context.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

tools.name: get_latest_release
tools.description: Returns the most recent release we’ve snapshotted for the specified repository. It refuses requests missing an owner or repo, and it refuses repositories that don’t exist or aren’t accessible. It also refuses the request when the repository has no releases to report.

tools.name: get_release_by_tag
tools.description: Returns the release in the specified repository that matches the provided tag name. It refuses requests missing owner, repo, or tag, and refuses tags that are empty or don’t match any release in that repository. It also refuses requests for repositories that don’t exist or aren’t accessible to the current integration context.

tag.description: Tag name (e.g., 'v1.0.0')

tools.name: get_label
tools.description: Returns a single label definition from the specified repository (name, color, description, and related metadata when available). It refuses requests missing owner, repo, or label name, and it refuses label names that don’t exist in that repository. It also refuses requests for repositories that don’t exist or aren’t accessible.

tools.name: list_commits
tools.description: Lists commits for a repository at the specified ref (sha/branch/tag) and returns a paginated set of commit summaries, optionally filtered by author. It refuses requests missing owner or repo, with pagination values outside the supported range (page < 1, perPage < 1, or perPage > 100), or with a sha/ref that doesn’t resolve in the repository. It also refuses requests for repositories that don’t exist or aren’t accessible to the current integration context.

author.description: Author username or email address to filter commits by

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

sha.description: Commit SHA, branch or tag name to list commits of. If not provided, uses the default branch of the repository. If a commit SHA is provided, will list commits up to that SHA.

tools.name: get_commit
tools.description: Returns details for a single commit identified by SHA, branch, or tag, and includes file diffs/stats when include_diff is true (default). It refuses requests missing owner, repo, or sha, and refuses sha values that don’t resolve to a commit in the repository. It also refuses requests for repositories that don’t exist or aren’t accessible, and refuses pagination values outside the supported range when diff output is paginated (page < 1, perPage < 1, or perPage > 100).

include_diff.description: Whether to include file diffs and stats in the response. Default is true.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

sha.description: Commit SHA, branch name, or tag name

tools.name: get_file_contents
tools.description: Returns the contents and metadata for a file, or a directory listing when the path points to a directory, using the repository’s default branch unless ref or sha is provided. It refuses requests missing owner or repo, and it refuses requests where both ref and sha are provided because they conflict. It also refuses paths or refs/shas that don’t exist in the repository, directories not expressed as directories (for example, a directory path that is not treated as a directory), and repositories that don’t exist or aren’t accessible.

path.description: Path to file/directory (directories must end with a slash '/')

ref.description: Accepts optional git refs such as `refs/tags/{tag}`, `refs/heads/{branch}` or `refs/pull/{pr_number}/head`

sha.description: Accepts optional commit SHA. If specified, it will be used instead of ref

tools.name: list_issues
tools.description: Lists issues we can retrieve for the specified repository and returns a paginated set of issue records, with optional filtering by state, labels, and since, and optional ordering via orderBy+direction. It refuses requests missing owner or repo, with perPage outside 1–100, or where only one of orderBy/direction is provided because sorting would be ambiguous. It also refuses invalid cursors, invalid enum values, malformed since timestamps, and repositories that don’t exist or aren’t accessible.

after.description: Cursor for pagination. Use the endCursor from the previous page's PageInfo for GraphQL APIs.

direction.description: Order direction. If provided, the 'orderBy' also needs to be provided.

labels.description: Filter by labels

orderBy.description: Order issues by field. If provided, the 'direction' also needs to be provided.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

since.description: Filter by date (ISO 8601 timestamp)

state.description: Filter by state, by default both open and closed issues are returned when not provided

tools.name: issue_read
tools.description: Performs a read operation on a single issue and returns either the issue details, its comments, its sub-issues, or its labels depending on method. It also refuses pagination values outside the supported range (page < 1, perPage < 1, or perPage > 100) for methods that page results, and refuses repositories/issues that aren’t accessible.

method.description:
The read operation to perform on a single issue.

2. get_comments - Get issue comments.
3. get_sub_issues - Get sub-issues of the issue.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

tools.name: issue_write
tools.description: Creates a new issue or updates an existing one (title/body/state/labels/assignees/milestone/type, and state_reason/duplicate_of when applicable) and returns the resulting issue record. It also refuses updates that the caller isn’t authorized to perform, label/assignee/milestone/type values that don’t exist in the repository’s context, and conflicting state inputs (for example, state_reason=duplicate without duplicate_of, or state_reason provided without a state change).

assignees.description: Usernames to assign to this issue

body.description: Issue body content

duplicate_of.description: Issue number that this issue is a duplicate of. Only used when state_reason is 'duplicate'.

labels.description: Labels to apply to this issue

method.description:
Write operation to perform on a single issue.
Options are: 
- 'create' - creates a new issue. 
- 'update' - updates an existing issue.

state_reason.description: Reason for the state change. Ignored unless state is changed.

type.description: Type of this issue. Only use if the repository has issue types configured. Use list_issue_types tool to get valid type values for the organization. If the repository doesn't support issue types, omit this parameter.

tools.name: sub_issue_write
tools.description: Adds, removes, or reorders a sub-issue under a parent issue in the specified repository, returning the updated sub-issue relationship/order for that parent issue. It refuses requests missing the required identifiers (owner, repo, issue_number, sub_issue_id) or using a method other than add, remove, or reprioritize. It also refuses reprioritize requests that don’t specify exactly one of after_id or before_id, add requests that attempt to attach a sub-issue that already has a different parent without replace_parent, and any operation where the referenced issues don’t exist in the repo or you don’t have permission to modify the parent issue.

after_id.description: The ID of the sub-issue to be prioritized after (either after_id OR before_id should be specified)

before_id.description: The ID of the sub-issue to be prioritized before (either after_id OR before_id should be specified)

issue_number.description: The number of the parent issue

method.description:
The action to perform on a single sub-issue
Options are:
- 'add' - add a sub-issue to a parent issue in a GitHub repository.
- 'remove' - remove a sub-issue from a parent issue in a GitHub repository.
- 'reprioritize' - change the order of sub-issues within a parent issue in a GitHub repository. Use either 'after_id' or 'before_id' to specify the new position.

replace_parent.description: When true, replaces the sub-issue's current parent issue. Use with 'add' method only.

sub_issue_id.description: The ID of the sub-issue to add. ID is not the same as issue number

tools.name: add_issue_comment

tools.name: list_pull_requests

tools.name: pull_request_read

method.description:

 2. get_diff - Get the diff of a pull request.

 6. get_reviews - Get the reviews on a pull request. When asked for review comments, use get_review_comments method.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (min 1, max 100)

tools.name: pull_request_review_write

It also refuses if the pull request doesn’t exist or is inaccessible, if you try to submit/delete when you have no pending review for that PR, or if you lack permission to review in the repository.

body.description: Review comment text

method.description: The write operation to perform on pull request review.

tools.name: add_comment_to_pending_review

body.description: The text of the review comment

line.description: The line of the blob in the pull request diff that the comment applies to. For multi-line comments, the last line of the range

path.description: The relative path to the file that necessitates a comment

project_id.description: ID of the project containing the task.

task_id.description: ID of the task to fetch.

tools.name: create_task
tools.description: Creates a task in the specified project for the specified user and returns the created task record; when `column_id` is provided the task is placed in that kanban column. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if required fields are missing/invalid, timestamps are not RFC3339/ISO-8601, or enums are invalid, UNAUTHORIZED if the API token is missing/invalid, FORBIDDEN if the token cannot create tasks for the given user/project, and NOT_FOUND if the project (or referenced column, when provided) does not exist. May raise CONFLICT if the task cannot be created due to an invalid project/column relationship, and may raise RATE_LIMITED when request quotas are exceeded.

project_id.description: ID of the project to create the task in.

user_id.description: ID of the user who owns the task.

column_id.description: ID of the kanban column to place the task in.

is_all_day.description: Whether the task is an all-day item.

sort_order.description: Manual sort order within the project/column.

tools.name: update_task
tools.description: Updates an existing task (including moving it to a different project and/or column) and returns the updated task record. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if IDs are malformed or any supplied fields are invalid, UNAUTHORIZED if the API token is missing/invalid, FORBIDDEN if the token cannot modify the task or the destination project/column, and NOT_FOUND if the task does not exist (or if a referenced destination project/column does not exist). Raises CONFLICT if the requested move/state change is not allowed (for example, moving a task to a column that does not belong to the target project), and may raise RATE_LIMITED when request quotas are exceeded.

task_id.description: ID of the task to update.

is_all_day.description: Whether the task is an all-day task.

project_id.description: Move the task to a different project.

column_id.description: Move the task to a different kanban column.

sort_order.description: Updated sort order within its list/column.

tools.name: complete_task
tools.description: Marks the specified task as completed and returns the updated task record; if `completed_at` is omitted the server sets it to the current time. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if `task_id` is malformed or `completed_at` is not a valid date-time, UNAUTHORIZED if the API token is missing/invalid, FORBIDDEN if the token cannot modify the task, and NOT_FOUND if the task does not exist. Raises CONFLICT if the task cannot be completed from its current state (for example, already completed or deleted), and may raise RATE_LIMITED when request quotas are exceeded.

task_id.description: ID of the task to mark as completed.

completed_at.description: Completion timestamp to set (RFC 3339); if omitted, server sets current time.

tools.name: delete_task
tools.description: Deletes the task identified by `task_id` and returns a confirmation of deletion (no task payload is returned). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if `task_id` does not match the required `tt_tsk_...` format, UNAUTHORIZED if the API token is missing/invalid, FORBIDDEN if the task is not owned by the authenticated user, and NOT_FOUND if no such task exists or it is not accessible.

task_id.description: ID of the task to delete.

tools.name: get_current_user

include_rate_limits.description: Whether to include current rate-limit/quota consumption in the response.

tools.name: get_project_tasks

column_id.description: Filter tasks by kanban column placement.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks to return.

importance_score.description: Importance score in [0,1]. Defaults to 0.5 when ingesting if omitted.

tools.description: Returns the authenticated account’s own user profile using the provided account_id, serving cached data unless refresh=true triggers a refetch and cache update; the response is the stored user record for that account context. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if account_id is missing/invalid, NOT_FOUND if the account_id does not exist locally, UNAUTHORIZED if the account is not usable for API access, and RATE_LIMITED if the upstream X quota for profile fetches is exhausted (including when refresh=true).

account_id.description: Local authenticated account id to use as context for fetching the profile.

refresh.description: Whether to force-refresh the profile from X instead of using cached data.

tools.name: browser_close
tools.description: Closes the currently active browser page for this captured session and returns once the page has been closed. It refuses the request if there is no active page to close or the session has already ended.

tools.name: browser_resize
tools.description: Resizes the captured browser window to the provided width and height and returns after the new viewport size is applied. It refuses requests missing width or height, with non-numeric values, or with non-positive dimensions. It also refuses the request if there is no active browser window for the current session.

tools.name: browser_console_messages
tools.description: Returns the console messages recorded for the current page in this session, optionally limited to errors when onlyErrors is true. It refuses the request if there is no active page/session to read messages from.

tools.name: browser_handle_dialog
tools.description: Responds to the currently open page dialog (alert/confirm/prompt) by accepting or dismissing it, and returns after the dialog is handled. It refuses the request if no dialog is currently open, or if promptText is provided when the dialog is not a prompt (or required by a prompt but missing). It may also refuse if the page is no longer active in this session.

promptText.description: The text of the prompt in case of a prompt dialog.

tools.name: browser_evaluate
tools.description: Evaluates the provided JavaScript function in the context of the current page, optionally passing the referenced element, and returns the evaluation result. It refuses requests without a function, with a function that cannot be parsed/executed, or that reference an element ref that does not exist in the latest snapshot. It also refuses element-scoped evaluation if the element is not available/attached or the session has no active page.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

function.description: () => { /* code */ } or (element) => { /* code */ } when element is provided

ref.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

tools.name: browser_file_upload
tools.description: Supplies files to the currently open file chooser for this page, or cancels the chooser when paths is omitted, and returns after the chooser is resolved. It refuses the request if no file chooser is currently open, if any provided path is not an absolute path, or if a referenced file cannot be read. It may also refuse if the page no longer has an active upload target in this session.

paths.description: The absolute paths to the files to upload. Can be single file or multiple files. If omitted, file chooser is cancelled.

tools.name: browser_fill_form
tools.description: Fills multiple form fields on the current page according to the provided field refs and values, and returns after the fills are applied. It refuses requests with missing fields, unknown field types, refs not present in the latest snapshot, or values that don’t match the target control (for example non-boolean checkbox values or combobox values that don’t map to an option). It also refuses if a field is not editable/disabled, not attached, or the session has no active page.

fields.description: Fields to fill in

ref.description: Exact target field reference from the page snapshot

value.description: Value to fill in the field. If the field is a checkbox, the value should be `true` or `false`. If the field is a combobox, the value should be the text of the option.

tools.name: browser_install
tools.description: Install the browser specified in the config. Call this if you get an error about the browser not being installed.

browser.description: Browser to install as specified by the service configuration.

tools.name: browser_press_key
tools.description: Sends a key press to the current page and returns after the key event is dispatched. It refuses requests without a key, with an empty key value, or when there is no active page to receive input in this session.

key.description: Name of the key to press or a character to generate, such as `ArrowLeft` or `a`

tools.name: browser_type
tools.description: Types the provided text into the referenced editable element, optionally typing slowly and/or submitting with Enter, and returns after input is performed. It refuses requests missing element, ref, or text, with a ref that is not found in the latest snapshot, or when the target is not an editable/attached element or is disabled. It also refuses if the page is not active or cannot receive input for this session.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

ref.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

slowly.description: Whether to type one character at a time. Useful for triggering key handlers in the page. By default entire text is filled in at once.

submit.description: Whether to submit entered text (press Enter after)

text.description: Text to type into the element

tools.name: browser_navigate
tools.description: Navigates the current page to the provided URL and returns after navigation is initiated/completed for the session. It refuses requests without a url, with a url that is not a valid URL, or that uses a disallowed/unsupported scheme. It also refuses the request if there is no active page to navigate in the current session.

url.description: The URL to navigate to

tools.name: browser_navigate_back
tools.description: Navigates the active tab back one step in its history and returns the updated browser state after navigation completes. It refuses the request when there is no active tab or there is no previous history entry to go back to. It may also refuse if the current page is no longer in a navigable state (for example, the session has ended).

tools.name: browser_network_requests
tools.description: Returns the network requests observed for the active tab since the current page load began. It refuses the request when there is no active tab or no page has been loaded in the current tab yet, because there is no request log to report against. It may also refuse when network tracking is not available for the session.

tools.name: browser_take_screenshot
tools.description: Captures an image of the current page and returns the captured screenshot result, either for the visible viewport, the full scrollable page, or a specific element. It refuses requests that specify only one of element/ref (both must be provided together for an element screenshot), and refuses requests that set fullPage together with an element screenshot because those modes conflict. It also refuses when the requested image type is not one of the supported formats or when there is no active page to capture.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to screenshot the element. If not provided, the screenshot will be taken of viewport. If element is provided, ref must be provided too.

filename.description: File name to save the screenshot to. Defaults to `page-{timestamp}.{png|jpeg}` if not specified. Prefer relative file names to stay within the output directory.

fullPage.description: When true, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Cannot be used with element screenshots.

ref.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot. If not provided, the screenshot will be taken of viewport. If ref is provided, element must be provided too.

type.description: Image format for the screenshot. Default is png.

tools.name: browser_snapshot
tools.description: Captures and returns an accessibility-focused snapshot of the current page state, optionally including console messages and/or network requests. It refuses the request when there is no active tab or no page is available to snapshot. It also refuses unknown fields in the request body because the snapshot options are strictly limited to the supported flags.

includeConsole.description: Whether to include console messages in the captured page state snapshot.

includeNetwork.description: Whether to include network requests in the captured page state snapshot.

tools.name: browser_click
tools.description: Clicks a specific page element identified by its snapshot reference and returns the resulting updated state after the interaction. It refuses the request when element/ref are missing, when the ref does not exist in the current snapshot, or when the element is not currently actionable (for example, detached, hidden, or disabled). It also refuses unsupported button values or modifier combinations that cannot be applied in the current environment.

button.description: Button to click, defaults to left

doubleClick.description: Whether to perform a double click instead of a single click

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

ref.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

tools.name: browser_drag
tools.description: Performs a drag-and-drop from the start element to the end element (both identified by snapshot references) and returns the updated state after the interaction. It refuses the request when any of startElement/startRef/endElement/endRef are missing, when either ref is not present in the current snapshot, or when either element cannot be interacted with at the time of the drag. It also refuses when the drag cannot be completed because the page changes or the elements become invalid during the operation.

endElement.description: Human-readable target element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element

endRef.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

startElement.description: Human-readable source element description used to obtain the permission to interact with the element

startRef.description: Exact source element reference from the page snapshot

tools.name: browser_hover
tools.description: Moves the pointer over a specific page element identified by its snapshot reference and returns the updated state after the hover. It refuses the request when element/ref are missing or when the ref does not match an element in the current snapshot. It also refuses when the element cannot be hovered (for example, it is not visible or has been removed from the page).

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

ref.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

tools.name: browser_select_option
tools.description: Selects one or more option values for a specific select control identified by its snapshot reference and returns the updated state after the selection. It refuses the request when element/ref/values are missing, when values is empty, when the ref does not exist in the current snapshot, or when the target is not a selectable control. It also refuses when any provided value does not correspond to an available option for that control or when multiple values are provided for a single-select element.

element.description: Human-readable element description used to obtain permission to interact with the element

ref.description: Exact target element reference from the page snapshot

values.description: Array of values to select in the dropdown. This can be a single value or multiple values.

tools.name: browser_tabs
tools.description: Lists tabs, creates a new tab, closes a tab, or selects an existing tab, and returns the resulting tab state after the action. It refuses requests with an unsupported action, and refuses close/select when the provided index does not refer to an existing tab (or when there is no current tab to close if index is omitted). It may also refuse to close the last remaining tab when the session requires at least one tab to stay open.

action.description: Operation to perform

index.description: Tab index, used for close/select. If omitted for close, current tab is closed.

tools.name: browser_wait_for
tools.description: Waits until the provided text appears, the provided textGone disappears, or the specified time elapses, and then returns the updated state when the wait condition is satisfied. It refuses the request when none of text, textGone, or time is provided because there is no wait condition to evaluate. It also refuses when time is negative or when both text and textGone are provided in a way that cannot be evaluated against the current page (for example, no active page to observe).

text.description: The text to wait for

textGone.description: The text to wait for to disappear

time.description: The time to wait in seconds

tools.name: slack_list_channels
tools.description: Lists channels in the workspace scoped by the given installation and returns a single page of cached channel records filtered by types and include_archived; pagination uses cursor and returns at most limit items along with a next cursor when more results are available. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if installation_id/cursor/limit/types are invalid, NOT_FOUND if the installation does not exist, and FORBIDDEN if the installation is not authorized to read channels in the workspace; may raise RATE_LIMITED when Slack or this service enforces request limits.

installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to scope the workspace.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for fetching the next page of channels.

limit.description: Maximum number of channels to return.

tools.name: slack_post_message
tools.description: Posts a new message to the specified cached channel using the OAuth tokens from the installation, persists the Slack message id/timestamp in the cache, and returns the created message record. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if ids are malformed, text is empty, or blocks/attachments payloads are invalid, NOT_FOUND if the installation or channel_id does not exist in the cache, and FORBIDDEN if the installation lacks permission to post to the channel; may raise RATE_LIMITED on quota exhaustion and CONFLICT if the channel is not in a postable state (e.g., archived).

installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to use for posting via the stored OAuth tokens.

channel_id.description: Internal cached channel id to post into.

text.description: Message text to post.

blocks.description: Slack Block Kit blocks payload to include with the message.

attachments.description: Slack legacy attachments payload to include with the message.

tools.name: slack_reply_to_thread
tools.description: Posts a reply to the thread whose parent is the given cached message id, persists the Slack reply id/timestamp and thread linkage, and returns the created reply message record. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if ids are malformed, text is empty, or blocks/attachments payloads are invalid, NOT_FOUND if the installation or parent_message_id is unknown, and CONFLICT if the parent message is not a threadable root in our cache; raises FORBIDDEN if the installation cannot post in that channel/thread and RATE_LIMITED when request limits are hit.

installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to use for posting via the stored OAuth tokens.

parent_message_id.description: Internal cached message id of the thread parent to reply to.

text.description: Reply text to post in the thread.

blocks.description: Slack Block Kit blocks payload to include with the reply.

attachments.description: Slack legacy attachments payload to include with the reply.

tools.name: slack_add_reaction
tools.description: Adds the given emoji reaction (by name, without colons) to the specified cached message via the installation’s OAuth tokens, updates the cached reactions, and returns the updated message/reaction state. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if ids are malformed or emoji_name is empty/invalid, NOT_FOUND if the installation or message_id does not exist, and FORBIDDEN if the installation cannot react in the message’s channel; raises CONFLICT if the reaction already exists or the message cannot be reacted to, and RATE_LIMITED when quotas are exceeded.

installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to use for reacting via the stored OAuth tokens.

message_id.description: Internal cached message id to add the reaction to.

emoji_name.description: Emoji name to add (without colons), e.g. thumbs_up.

tools.name: slack_get_channel_history
tools.description: Returns a paged list of cached messages for the given cached channel, filtered by oldest/latest and inclusive, ordered as Slack history is returned; pagination uses cursor and returns up to limit messages with a next cursor when more are available. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if ids/cursor/limit or oldest/latest values are invalid, NOT_FOUND if the installation or channel_id is unknown, and FORBIDDEN if the installation is not authorized to read that channel’s history; may raise RATE_LIMITED under request throttling.

installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to scope the workspace.

channel_id.description: Internal cached channel id to read message history from.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for fetching the next page of messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return.

oldest.description: Only include messages with Slack ts greater than or equal to this value.

latest.description: Only include messages with Slack ts less than or equal to this value.

inclusive.description: Whether to include messages exactly at oldest/latest boundaries.

tools.name: slack_get_thread_replies
tools.description: Returns a paged list of cached replies for the thread rooted at parent_message_id, filtered by oldest/latest and inclusive; pagination uses cursor and returns up to limit replies with a next cursor when more are available. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if ids/cursor/limit or oldest/latest values are invalid, NOT_FOUND if the installation or parent_message_id is unknown, and CONFLICT if the referenced message is not a thread parent in our cache; raises FORBIDDEN if the installation cannot read the thread and RATE_LIMITED when throttled.

installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to scope the workspace.

parent_message_id.description: Internal cached message id of the thread parent to fetch replies for.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for fetching the next page of replies.

limit.description: Maximum number of replies to return.

oldest.description: Only include replies with Slack ts greater than or equal to this value.

latest.description: Only include replies with Slack ts less than or equal to this value.

inclusive.description: Whether to include replies exactly at oldest/latest boundaries.

installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to scope the workspace.

tools.name: slack_get_user_profile

installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to scope the workspace.

user_id.description: Internal cached user id to fetch detailed profile information for.

tools.name: slack_sync_workspace
tools.description: Synchronizes cached workspace state (users and channels, and optionally message history) for the given installation by calling Slack APIs using the stored OAuth tokens, upserting records, updating last_synced_at fields, and returning a summary of created/updated counts. installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to sync.

sync_messages.description: Whether to sync message history into slack_messages.

channel_ids.description: If provided, restrict message sync to these cached channel ids.

oldest.description: When syncing messages, only fetch messages at or after this Slack timestamp.

latest.description: When syncing messages, only fetch messages at or before this Slack timestamp.

limit_per_channel.description: When syncing messages, maximum messages to fetch per channel per run.

tools.name: slack_update_installation_status
tools.description: Transitions an installation lifecycle status (active/disabled/revoked) and returns the updated installation record. installation_id.description: Slack installation record id to update.

status.description: New lifecycle status for the installation.

last_api_error.description: Optional last API error message to store for diagnostics.

tools.name: slack_whoami
tools.description: Returns the caller identity and authorization context for this MCP server, including the resolved active installation (if any), granted scopes, and current quota/rate-limit consumption known to the service. If client_key is provided, at most one non-archived session may exist for that client_key; the service will reuse an existing active/cleared session or archive the previous one before creating a new session. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for invalid inputs and CONFLICT if the requested status transition cannot be satisfied.

client_key.description: Optional client-provided key used to bind a session to a stable client identity; must map to at most one non-archived session.

reuse_existing.description: When true (default server behavior), reuses an existing non-archived session for the given client_key if present; when false, forces creation and archives any prior non-archived session with the same client_key.

tools.name: update_session
tools.description: Updates mutable fields on the current session, including driving allowed lifecycle transitions on status. Returns the updated session. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if there is no active session context, NOT_FOUND if the session does not exist, VALIDATION_ERROR for invalid field values, and CONFLICT if the requested status transition is not allowed (active↔cleared, active/cleared→archived; archived is terminal).

status.description: New session status. Must follow allowed transitions: active→cleared/archived, cleared→active/archived; archived is terminal.

tools.name: delete_thought
tools.description: Soft-deletes a single thought in the current session by id (sets status=deleted and deleted_at) and returns the deleted thought record. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if there is no active session context, NOT_FOUND if the thought does not exist in the current session, and CONFLICT if the thought is already deleted or cannot transition from its current status.

thought_id.description: The id of the thought to delete; must belong to the current session.

tools.name: rollback_clear
tools.description: Rolls back the most recent soft clear operation for the current session by transitioning the latest session_resets record from applied→rolled_back and restoring the session to active. Returns the rollback record and the restored session stats. Raises UNAUTHORIZED if there is no active session context, NOT_FOUND if there is no applicable applied reset to roll back, and CONFLICT if the reset is not in a rollback-eligible state or if the session is archived.

reset_id.description: Optional specific session_resets id to roll back; if omitted, rolls back the most recent applied reset for the current session.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Returns the calling identity as derived from the presented API key and the caller’s current entitlements and rate-limit consumption. Refuses UNAUTHORIZED when no valid credential is presented or the key is revoked.

api_key.description: API key credential used to authenticate the caller; if omitted, the service will attempt to use the ambient credential bound to the current context.

tools.name: get_active_file
tools.description: Returns the file currently marked as active for the given session, optionally including the latest content snapshot when include_content is true. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if session_id/vault_id format is invalid, NOT_FOUND if the session does not exist or (when vault_id is provided) the session is not in that vault, and NOT_FOUND if the session has no active file or the active file record no longer exists. Raises FORBIDDEN if the caller is not allowed to access the session/vault.

session_id.description: Obsidian integration session id whose active file should be returned.

vault_id.description: Vault id to scope the session lookup (used to disambiguate in multi-vault setups).

include_content.description: Whether to include the active file's current content in the response.

tools.name: delete_active_file
tools.description: Deletes the file currently marked as active for the given session, performing a soft delete by default or a permanent removal when hard_delete is true, and records the reason in the audit trail when provided. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if inputs are malformed, NOT_FOUND if the session does not exist, the session has no active file, or the active file cannot be found in the specified vault scope, and CONFLICT if the file is already deleted (soft delete) or cannot be hard-deleted due to its current lifecycle state. Raises FORBIDDEN if the caller is not allowed to delete files in the session’s vault.

session_id.description: Session id whose currently active file should be deleted.

vault_id.description: Vault id that contains the active file.

hard_delete.description: If true, remove the file record/content permanently; otherwise mark as deleted (soft delete).

reason.description: Optional audit reason for deleting the active file.

tools.name: insert_active_file
tools.description: Applies a deterministic edit to the active file for the given session by inserting or replacing text relative to the provided selector (heading, block, or frontmatter) and returns the updated file metadata (and updated content snapshot where supported). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for invalid selector/type/position or missing required fields, NOT_FOUND if the session or active file does not exist (or does not belong to vault_id when provided) or if the selector target cannot be located in the current document, and CONFLICT if expected_sha256 is provided and does not match the current content hash or if the file is deleted. Raises FORBIDDEN if the caller cannot edit the session’s active file.

session_id.description: Session id whose active file will be modified.

vault_id.description: Vault id that contains the active file.

selector.description: Target selector describing where to apply the modification (e.g., heading, block reference, or frontmatter field).

type.description: Selector type used to locate the insertion target.

value.description: Selector value (e.g., heading text, block id/reference, or frontmatter key).

position.description: How to apply the insertion relative to the selected target.

text.description: Markdown text payload to insert/replace at the selected location.

expected_sha256.description: If provided, the operation will only apply if the current file content hash matches (optimistic concurrency).

tools.name: append_active_file
tools.description: Appends text to the end of the session’s active file (ensuring a preceding newline when ensure_newline is true) and returns the updated file metadata (and updated content snapshot where supported). Raises VALIDATION_ERROR for malformed inputs, NOT_FOUND if the session does not exist or has no active file (or the active file is not in vault_id when provided), and CONFLICT if expected_sha256 is provided and does not match the current content hash or if the file is deleted. Raises FORBIDDEN if the caller is not allowed to modify the active file.

session_id.description: Session id whose active file will be appended to.

vault_id.description: Vault id that contains the active file.

text.description: Markdown text to append to the end of the active file.

ensure_newline.description: If true, ensures there is a newline before appending text.

expected_sha256.description: If provided, the append will only apply if the current file content hash matches (optimistic concurrency).

tools.name: open_file
tools.description: Sets the session’s active file by opening an existing file by file_id or by vault-relative path, and returns the session’s updated active_file_id and the opened file’s metadata. Raises VALIDATION_ERROR if neither file_id nor path is provided, if both are provided inconsistently, or if any id format is invalid; NOT_FOUND if the vault does not exist, if file_id does not exist in the vault, or if the path does not resolve to a file and create_if_missing is not true. session_id.description: Session id to associate with opening the file (sets active_file_id).

vault_id.description: Vault id that contains the file to open.

file_id.description: File id to open in Obsidian.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the file to open (alternative to file_id).

create_if_missing.description: If true and path is provided, create the file if it does not exist.

tools.name: insert_file
tools.description: Applies a deterministic edit to a specific file (by file_id or path) by inserting or replacing text relative to the provided selector (heading, block, or frontmatter) and returns the updated file metadata (and updated content snapshot where supported), attributing the change to session_id when provided. Raises CONFLICT if expected_sha256 is provided and does not match the current content hash or if the file is deleted, and FORBIDDEN if the caller cannot edit files in the vault.

vault_id.description: Vault id that contains the file to modify.

path.description: Vault-relative path of the file to modify (alternative to file_id).

session_id.description: Optional session id to attribute this edit operation for audit/history.

selector.description: Target selector describing where to apply the modification (e.g., heading, block reference, or frontmatter field).

type.description: Selector type used to locate the insertion target.

value.description: Selector value (e.g., heading text, block id/reference, or frontmatter key).

position.description: How to apply the insertion relative to the selected target.

text.description: Markdown text payload to insert/replace at the selected location.

expected_sha256.description: If provided, the operation will only apply if the current file content hash matches (optimistic concurrency).

session_id.description: Optional session id to associate the search query for audit/history.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor for fetching the next page of results.

vault_id.description: Vault id whose directory contents should be listed.

include_deleted.description: If true, include files marked deleted in the integration database.

limit.description: Maximum number of files to return.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor for fetching the next page of files.
